encounters.cc: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and nonproductive cough for 6 months

lines: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and nonproductive cough for 6 months
His medications include lisinopril and omeprazole.
He has never smoked and has no known occupational exposures.
He denies any recent infections, chest pain, or leg swelling.
Oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
On physical examination, fine inspiratory crackles are heard at the lung bases bilaterally.
High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest shows subpleural reticular opacities with honeycombing but no evidence of emphysema or nodules.
Pulmonary function tests reveal a restrictive pattern with reduced forced vital capacity (FVC) and a normal forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)/FVC ratio.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue and decreased exercise tolerance

lines: Progressive fatigue and decreased exercise tolerance
The patient with a history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis returns for hematology evaluation approximately three months following his prior pulmonology encounter.
He presents with progressive fatigue and decreased exercise tolerance over the past several months.
He denies recent blood loss, changes in bowel habits, or melena.
He mentions occasional numbness and tingling in his feet and difficulty concentrating at work.
He has a history of hypertension and epilepsy.
He takes for which he takes lisinopril and phenytoin.
He reports frequent alcohol use and says he drinks "about a six-pack" most evenings to help him unwind.
He lives alone and admits that his diet consists mostly of boxed and canned foods.
On review of systems, he denies fever, weight loss, or night sweats.
Physical exam shows pallor and mild ataxia.
Neurologic testing reveals decreased vibratory sense and ankle reflexes bilaterally.
Cardiac and pulmonary exams are normal.
Laboratory tests reveal a normocytic anemia.
Iron studies show elevated serum iron, increased ferritin, and decreased total iron-binding capacity.
Alcohol: Heavy daily use (6-10 standard drinks/day, primarily beer, for 30+ years).
Jugular venous distension, bibasilar crackles, a third heart sound (S3), and a laterally displaced point of maximal impulse
Echocardiography demonstrates global hypokinesis and left ventricular dilation.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with severe alcohol use disorder, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, sideroblastic anemia, and tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy who presents with acute neurological symptoms.
He is brought to the emergency department by his wife due to new-onset confusion and difficulty walking over the past 24 hours.
He was discharged from hospital three days ago after elective right knee arthroplasty.
His postoperative course was uneventful, and he had been recovering well until yesterday.
He takes atenolol for hypertension and has taken one dose of oxycodone in the last 24 hours.
His wife reports that he has a long history of daily alcohol consumption, drinking 6–10 cans of beer per day for many years, although he initially denied this to the surgical team.
On examination, the patient is afebrile, with a blood pressure of 125/76 mm Hg, pulse of 88/min, and respiratory rate of 15/min.
He is alert but disoriented to time and place.
He cannot recall three simple objects after a few minutes and needs repeated prompting to follow commands.
He has a wide-based gait and horizontal nystagmus with limited abduction of the right eye.
Laboratory studies, including complete blood count, serum electrolytes, glucose, and renal and hepatic function, are within normal limits.

encounters.cc: 2-week history of low-grade fever, malaise, and productive cough with foul-smelling sputum

lines: 2-week history of low-grade fever, malaise, and productive cough with foul-smelling sputum

The patient is a 68-year-old male with severe alcohol use disorder, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and recurrent aspiration who presents to the Emergency Department six months following an episode of Wernicke encephalopathy.
He reports a recent episode of "choking on food" while drinking heavily.
History of chronic alcoholism and poor dental hygiene
On examination, he is afebrile, blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 92 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air
Lung auscultation reveals crackles at the right lower lung base.
Neurological examination shows a decreased gag reflex.
Chest X-ray: Infiltrate in the right lower lobe

encounters.cc: Fever, malaise, and productive cough with foul-smelling sputum for 3 weeks

lines: Fever, malaise, and productive cough with foul-smelling sputum for 3 weeks
The patient returns with recurrent symptoms similar to his prior aspiration event.
He presents to the emergency department with a 3-week history of fever, malaise, and productive cough with foul-smelling sputum and reports a recent episode of loss of consciousness while drinking.
Alcohol: Heavy daily use (6-10 standard drinks/day, primarily beer, for 30+ years).
On examination, his temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), heart rate is 102 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air
Lung auscultation reveals decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at the right lung base
Chest radiography shows a cavitary lesion in the right lower lobe with an air-fluid level

encounters.cc: Acute onset of shortness of breath and cough

lines: Acute onset of shortness of breath and cough
The patient returns following prior aspiration pneumonia and lung abscess, presenting with acute onset of shortness of breath and cough after a witnessed episode of vomiting
Alcohol: Heavy daily use (6-10 standard drinks/day, primarily beer, for 30+ years).
His temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), blood pressure is 155/90 mmHg, heart rate is 110 beats/min, respiratory rate is 28 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air
He appears anxious and is using accessory muscles to breathe.
Physical examination reveals bilateral crackles in the lower lung fields.

encounters.cc: Acute onset of shortness of breath and cough after large meal

lines: Acute onset of shortness of breath and cough after large meal

This 70-year-old male with recurrent aspiration, prior aspiration pneumonias, and poor dentition presents with acute onset of shortness of breath and cough that began several hours after a large meal.
He reports that he was lying down after eating when he suddenly experienced a bout of severe coughing and choking.
Alcohol: Heavy daily use (6-10 standard drinks/day, primarily beer, for 30+ years).
Temperature is 37.8°C, blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats/min, respiratory rate is 26 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation is 89% on room air
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral crackles, more prominent in the right lower lobe
Arterial blood gas on room air shows:
Chest X-ray shows bilateral alveolar infiltrates with a predilection for the right lower lobe
